title: fix(cli,driver-sql): defer migrate DDL until confirmed + detect SQLite occupancy (#3917)
body:
Closes #3917.

`os migrate plan` documented itself as a dry run and `os migrate apply` gated on a `[y/N]` prompt, but both booted the full plugin set first — and boot schema-sync issued create-table/add-column DDL (plus the artifact's inline seed wrote rows) against the target database before either promise was kept. Neither command asked whether anything else was using the database, which on a dev machine is usually a live `os dev`/`os serve` holding the same SQLite file.

## Deferred schema DDL (issue point 2)

- `SqlDriver` gains `setDeferredDdl` / `previewDeferredSchemaWork` / `flushDeferredSchemaDdl`. While armed, `initObjects` still registers every in-memory map drift detection depends on (`managedObjectFields`, coercion maps, tenancy) but **records** the physical work instead of performing it — including the `_objectstack_sequences` DDL that rode outside the per-object loop.
- `bootSchemaStack({ deferSchemaDdl: true })` arms it from a plugin whose `init()` depends on `com.objectstack.runtime.default-datasource`. The kernel runs every `init()` (Phase 1) before any `start()` (Phase 2), and `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` is where `syncRegisteredSchemas` runs — so that is the one window where the driver exists and no DDL has happened. It also passes `skipSeedData`, so the boot writes no rows either.
- `plan` and `apply` render the held-back work as a `New (additive)` section; `apply` counts it in the prompt and performs it via `flushSchemaDdl()` **only after confirmation**. `os meta resync` / `os migrate files-to-references` keep the old behaviour — they need the tables to exist.

## SQLite occupancy detection (issue point 1)

The issue suggested `-wal`/`-shm` presence plus a PRAGMA probe. Measured first, which changed the design:

| probe | nobody attached | attached but idle | open read txn | open write txn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-shm` present | no | **yes** | yes | yes |
| `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` busy | 0 | **0** | 0 | 1 |
| `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` | ok | **BUSY** | BUSY | BUSY |

`wal_checkpoint` only sees an *active writer*, missing the common case (a dev server idle between requests). Sidecar presence alone cannot tell a live server from a crashed one. So the probe is `PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE` + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` under `busy_timeout = 0`, which reports `SQLITE_BUSY` when another connection is **attached**, not merely writing. Non-destructive: an empty transaction, rolled back, locking mode restored. Rollback-journal databases degrade honestly to write-lock detection; a probe that cannot run at all returns `unknown` and never blocks the command.

Probed **before** boot — after it, our own pool is what the probe would find. `apply` refuses with exit 1 / `error: database_busy` unless `--force`; `plan` only warns, since it now writes nothing either way.

Also exports `resolveStandaloneDatabase()` from `@objectstack/runtime` so the CLI resolves the target file with the same precedence the boot uses — probing a different file than the one about to be migrated would be worse than not probing.

## Tests

25 new tests. The end-to-end one asserts that after a real `bootSchemaStack`, the database's tables, columns and row counts are each unchanged; the probe comparison table above is encoded as tests so a future switch back to the checkpoint probe fails.

- `packages/plugins/driver-sql` — 415 passed (42 files)
- `packages/cli` — 792 passed (76 files)
- `packages/runtime` — 720 passed (51 files)
- build + eslint clean on touched files

## Note for reviewers

The artifact's inline seed is suppressed on this boot too (`skipSeedData`). The issue only named DDL, but the same boot writes demo rows into the operator's live database — same class of problem. If that reads as out of scope, dropping the `skipSeedData` hunks leaves the rest working.
